LABEL: perceptual taste quality
A IAO:0000115: A quality of a material entity that is realised when a human perceiver tastes that entity.

LABEL: basic taste quality
A IAO:0000115: A perceptual taste quality for which a dedicated class of human taste receptor and a dedicated transduction pathway are established.

LABEL: sweetness
A IAO:0000115: The basic taste quality typically elicited by sucrose and other sugars, transduced by the TAS1R2 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.
A rdfs:comment: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

LABEL: sourness
A IAO:0000115: The basic taste quality typically elicited by citric acid and other acids, transduced by proton-sensitive channels of taste receptor cells.
A rdfs:comment: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

LABEL: saltiness
A IAO:0000115: The basic taste quality typically elicited by sodium chloride, transduced principally by the epithelial sodium channel.
A rdfs:comment: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

LABEL: bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The basic taste quality typically elicited by quinine and by many plant alkaloids and glycosides, transduced by the TAS2R receptor family.
A rdfs:comment: Mapped to PATO:0002474 by skos:exactMatch in mappings/hto-pato.sssom.tsv.

LABEL: umami
A IAO:0000115: The basic taste quality typically elicited by L-glutamate and by certain ribonucleotides, transduced by the TAS1R1 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.
A rdfs:comment: PATO has no term for this quality as of 2026-09-17; proposed to PATO.

LABEL: candidate taste quality
A IAO:0000115: A perceptual taste quality that has been proposed as basic but for which receptor or transduction evidence remains contested.
A rdfs:comment: Grouped separately so that including these terms does not commit a user of HTO to the claim that they are basic tastes.

LABEL: fattiness
A IAO:0000115: The candidate taste quality elicited by non-esterified fatty acids, proposed under the name oleogustus and distinct from the texture of fat.

LABEL: kokumi
A IAO:0000115: The candidate taste quality described as mouthfulness, continuity and thickness, elicited by certain gamma-glutamyl peptides acting on the calcium-sensing receptor.

LABEL: metallic taste
A IAO:0000115: The candidate taste quality elicited by certain metal salts and reported as a side effect of some medications.

LABEL: calcium taste
A IAO:0000115: The candidate taste quality elicited by calcium salts, reported as chalky and somewhat bitter.

LABEL: starchy taste
A IAO:0000115: The candidate taste quality elicited by oligomeric glucose polymers independently of sweetness.

LABEL: bitterness subtype
A IAO:0000115: A bitterness distinguished by the chemical class of the compound that elicits it and, where known, by the receptor that detects it.

LABEL: thiourea bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The bitterness elicited by compounds bearing a thiourea group, notably phenylthiocarbamide and propylthiouracil, detected by TAS2R38.
A rdfs:comment: The quality whose perception varies most sharply between people.

LABEL: limonoid bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The bitterness elicited by limonoid triterpenoids, notably limonin, which forms from a tasteless precursor after citrus fruit is juiced.

LABEL: flavanone bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The bitterness elicited by flavanone glycosides, notably naringin, characteristic of grapefruit and pomelo.

LABEL: alkaloid bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The bitterness elicited by plant alkaloids such as quinine and caffeine.

LABEL: amino acid bitterness
A IAO:0000115: The bitterness elicited by hydrophobic amino acids and by peptides rich in them, prominent in protein hydrolysates and aged cheese.

LABEL: chemesthetic quality
A IAO:0000115: A quality perceived in the mouth through the trigeminal nerve rather than through taste receptor cells, recorded alongside taste by sensory panels.
A rdfs:comment: Not a taste sensu stricto. Included because panels record it and because astringency is central to citrus assessment.

LABEL: astringency
A IAO:0000115: The chemesthetic quality of drying, roughening and puckering in the mouth, elicited by tannins and other polyphenols binding salivary proteins.
A rdfs:comment: CHEBI:74783 astringent exists but denotes a chemical role, not a perceptual quality.

LABEL: pungency
A IAO:0000115: The chemesthetic quality of burning or stinging, elicited by capsaicinoids, piperine and allyl isothiocyanate.

LABEL: cooling sensation
A IAO:0000115: The chemesthetic quality of coolness in the absence of a temperature change, elicited by menthol and related compounds.

LABEL: tingling sensation
A IAO:0000115: The chemesthetic quality of vibration or numbness, elicited by alkylamides such as sanshool.

LABEL: carbonation bite
A IAO:0000115: The chemesthetic quality elicited by dissolved carbon dioxide, mediated in part by carbonic anhydrase on trigeminal fibres.

LABEL: temporal taste quality
A IAO:0000115: A perceptual taste quality defined by when it appears or how long it persists relative to the stimulus entering the mouth.

LABEL: taste onset latency
A IAO:0000115: The temporal taste quality of how long after the stimulus enters the mouth a taste is first perceived.

LABEL: aftertaste
A IAO:0000115: The temporal taste quality of a taste that persists after the stimulus has been swallowed or expectorated.

LABEL: lingering bitterness
A IAO:0000115: An aftertaste that is bitter in quality.

LABEL: delayed bitterness
A IAO:0000115: A bitterness that is absent or weak when the stimulus is first tasted and appears or strengthens over subsequent minutes to hours.
A rdfs:comment: Characteristic of citrus juice, where limonin forms after juicing.

LABEL: taste adaptation
A IAO:0000115: The temporal taste quality of a perceived intensity declining during continued exposure to an unchanging stimulus.

LABEL: hedonic taste quality
A IAO:0000115: A quality of a stimulus consisting in how much a perceiver likes or dislikes tasting it, as distinct from what they perceive.

LABEL: palatability
A IAO:0000115: The hedonic taste quality of being pleasant to taste for a given perceiver.

LABEL: taste aversion
A IAO:0000115: The hedonic taste quality of being unpleasant to taste for a given perceiver, whether innately or through learning.
